lean.statement:
@anonymous_statement : ∀ {n N : ℕ} (f : SphereConfiguration n N → ℝ)
  (V : Fin N → SphereConfiguration n N → SphereAmbient n),
  ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 1 f →
    (∀ (i : Fin N), ContMDiff (sphereProductModel n N) 𝓘(ℝ, SphereAmbient n) 1 (V i)) →
      (∀ (x : SphereConfiguration n N) (i : Fin N), ⟪↑(x i), V i x⟫ = 0) →
        Integrable (sphereProductDivergence V) (sphereProductMeasure n N) ∧
          Integrable (fun x => f x * sphereProductDivergence V x) (sphereProductMeasure n N) ∧
            Integrable (fun x => ∑ i, ⟪sphereProductGradient f i x, V i x⟫) (sphereProductMeasure n N) ∧
              ∫ (x : SphereConfiguration n N), sphereProductDivergence V x ∂sphereProductMeasure n N = 0 ∧
                ∫ (x : SphereConfiguration n N), f x * sphereProductDivergence V x ∂sphereProductMeasure n N =
                  -∫ (x : SphereConfiguration n N), ∑ i, ⟪sphereProductGradient f i x, V i x⟫ ∂sphereProductMeasure n N

blind_reconstruction.text:
For arbitrary natural numbers n and N, put E=R^(n+1) with its Euclidean inner product, S={z in E: ||z||=1}, and C=S^(Fin N). No positivity hypothesis on n or N is present. C carries the product of the sphere charted-space instances displayed in the compiler output, with source model sphereProductModel n N = product_i R^n. In the regularity conditions below, C^k means precisely ContMDiff of order k for this source model and the self model on the indicated real vector-space target.

The integration measure is fixed by the following definitions. Write H=homeomorphUnitSphereProd E, a homeomorphism E\{0} -> S x (0,infinity). The supplied characterization identifies its first component as z/||z||. Let sigma=volume.toSphere on S, literally
 sigma = (n+1) * first_marginal( (comap(g,volume_E)) restricted to S x {r in (0,infinity): r<1} ),
where g=Subtype.val composed with H inverse and the displayed scalar denotes scaling of a measure. Let mu_1=sigma(S)^(-1) * sigma, with the inverse and scalar multiplication in the extended nonnegative reals as in the supplied definition, and let mu be the Fin N product of mu_1. This is the exact normalized polar angular-measure construction in the packet. No separate arbitrary measure or density is a theorem parameter.

For x in C, i in Fin N and y in S, x[i<-y] means replacing only the ith coordinate of x by y. For a scalar or E-valued function a on S define its literal radial extension R(a):E -> target by
 R(a)(z)=a(z/||z||) if z!=0, and R(a)(0)=0.
The zero value is part of the definition, not a smoothness assertion at the origin.

For a real function u on C define the ith vector G_i u(x) as follows. Set u_(i,x)(y)=u(x[i<-y]). Take the real ambient gradient of R(u_(i,x)) at the ambient vector x_i, and orthogonally project it onto (R x_i)^perp:
 G_i u(x)=P_(x_i) grad_E R(u_(i,x))(x_i),
 P_(x_i) a = a-<x_i,a>x_i.
Here the ambient gradient is literally the inverse Riesz map applied to fderiv_R. The supplied projection characterizations justify the displayed P formula and its values in x_i^perp.

For a family W_i:C -> E define
 Div W(x)=sum_(i in Fin N) sum_(k in Fin(n+1))
   lineDeriv_R [z -> (R(y -> W_i(x[i<-y]))(z))_k] (x_i) e_k,
where e_k is the kth standard Euclidean basis vector. Thus each component field is radially extended in its own sphere coordinate while the other configuration coordinates are held fixed. The supplied coordinate-divergence theorem identifies the inner sum with the diagonal trace sum of the Frechet derivative when that ambient extension is differentiable at x_i. These G_i and Div are exactly the defined sphereProductGradient and sphereProductDivergence operators; no independent intrinsic Riemannian, covariant-divergence, Hausdorff-measure or Wasserstein API identification is substituted for these definitions.

Let f:C -> R and V:Fin N -> C -> E be arbitrary. Assume f is C^1, each full-configuration map V_i:C -> E is C^1, and
 <x_i,V_i(x)>=0 for every x in C and every i in Fin N.
The last assumption is everywhere orthogonality to the unit normal; it is not merely an almost-everywhere or integrated condition.

Then all three real functions
 x -> Div V(x),
 x -> f(x) Div V(x),
 x -> sum_i <G_i f(x),V_i(x)>
are integrable with respect to mu. In addition, the following two exact real integral identities hold over all C:
 integral_C Div V dmu=0,
 integral_C f Div V dmu = - integral_C sum_i <G_i f,V_i> dmu.

Integrability is a conclusion, not an input. All inner products are the real Euclidean inner product on E. The assumptions concern the entire compact configuration domain, not a time interval or a set modulo null sets. The functions and operators are literal pointwise functions; there are no chosen Lp representatives. The integrals use the specified product measure, and the displayed equalities are scalar integral equalities. The finite sum is unnormalized: no factor 1/N occurs. The quantifier order is forall n,N, forall f,V, followed by the three assumptions and the five simultaneous conclusions. There are no existential constants, unspecified estimates, support assumptions, time horizons or convergence assertions.
